transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-11-30
Start: 16:00:00 UTC
Duration: 62 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Blake (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Marco Silva (Redwood CSM); Elena Ruiz (Morningstar Head of ML), Tom Carlson (VP Eng), Aisha Khan (Security/Cloud Architect), Ravi Patel (Data Engineer)

Auto-generated summary: Kickoff focused on inference SLAs, network architecture, and pilot scope. Action items recorded.

[00:00] Jordan: ok, hey everyone, thanks for jumping on. i'm Jordan from Redwood, i'm the AE on this account. quick intros, then we'll run through the 30k foot plan for week zero.
[00:14] Elena: hi all, Elena here, Head of ML at Morningstar HealthTech. excited to get this going.
[00:18] Tom: Tom Carlson, VP Eng. we'll be owning the infra bits.
[00:22] Aisha: Aisha, i run cloud security. i'll be the main reviewer for SSO/KMS and the audit path.
[00:27] Ravi: ravi, data eng, will help prep datasets and integration.
[00:31] Priya: priya, solutions engineer at Redwood. i'll lead the technical onboarding and benchmarks.
[00:36] Marco: marco, customer success, i'll coordinate the schedule and retention playbook.
[00:40] Jordan: cool, thanks. goal today -- align on success criteria for the pilot: target p95 latency under 120ms for 1k token responses, throughput for batch jobs, and no raw PHI leaving customer network. also map out network connectivity and next steps.
[00:56] Elena: two clarifications — 1) our clinical summarization model averages 800 tokens output, 2) data must be encrypted and reside in our eu-west-1 footprint for the pilot.
[01:08] Aisha: also SOC2 is table stakes; we'll need audit logs and KMS integration. can you describe Redwood's key management options? 
[01:18] Priya: sure, we have three common patterns: hosted where keys are managed by Redwood, customer-managed KMS via cloud KMS/HSM, or bring-your-own-key with HSM connectors. for private deployments we support full KMS control; for hosted we can integrate a CMK in customer account — there's a small handshake for rotation policies. sorry, small, there's a small bit of setup.
[01:39] Tom: when you say private deployment, do you mean on-prem or VPC? what are the latency tradeoffs?
[01:46] Priya: good q. private can be either VPC-based in our marketplace region or on-prem if you want air-gapped. VPC peering usually gives best latency and no egress to public internet; on-prem adds ops complexity but full data residency. in our experience VPC peering keeps p95 within 10-20ms of hosted in the same region, depending on prefix caching and batch profile.
[02:09] Elena: our priority is consistent p95 under 120ms. cost is secondary but not negligible. we also need to validate model quality after any quantizashun.
[02:18] Priya: absolutely — we can run the same evals pre/post quant to ensure no regressions. we have an optimize module that suggests quant profiles by workload.
[02:27] [02:30] Jordan: quick agenda check — i'll walk through the timeline, priya will cover technical plan, marco will talk ops cadence, then q&a and next steps. sound good?
[02:40] Elena: yes.
[02:42] Jordan: timeline: week 0 — staging access and security handshake; week 1 — perf benchmarks and integration priming; weeks 2–4 — pilot with canary rollout and quality evals; goal production by mid-q1.
[02:57] Tom: mid-q1 aligns w our release calendar. any blockers we should call out now?
[03:04] Priya: blockers typically: network firewall rules, service account provisioning for peering, and dataset anonymization. we'll send a checklist.
[03:12] Aisha: can you show me the peering checklist now?
[03:15] Priya: i'll share a doc after the call. top items: allow ports 443 and peering CIDR, routes for private endpoints, and mutual TLS for our control plane connections when required. also we recommend using a transit gateway for multi-vpc shops.
[03:34] [03:40] Ravi: about datasets — we'll anonymize PII but preserve clinical tokens. what's your preferred ingestion format?
[03:46] Priya: newline-delimited JSON is easiest for our pipeline. include token length metadata so we can simulate sequence lengths for batching.
[03:56] Jordan: ok, on the security front, a lot of customers ask about SAML and RBAC. Marco, quick note?
[04:02] Marco: Redwood supports SAML SSO with SCIM sync and role-based access. audit logs retained for 90 days by default and extended retention is an add-on. we can also push logs to customer SIEM via an event-forwarder.
[04:18] Aisha: 90 days is fine for now but we'll need a retention policy for 13 months later; want to capture how that's priced.
[04:26] Jordan: noted — marco will hoist pricing options.
[04:29] [04:34] Tom: can we talk about tokenization? we currently use a custom tokenizer with rare medical tokens. will that break embeddings / rerank flows?
[04:42] Priya: we can accept custom tokenization; for embedding parity it's important to supply a token map. otherwise we'll default to our tokenizer which may split tokens. for reranking we recommend providing question/answer pairs for evals.
[04:57] Elena: our initial workload: clinical note summarization and triage classification. expect bursts of 200 qps for triage spikes.
[05:07] Priya: for bursty traffic we'll suggest a dedicated pool with autoscaling headroom or a hybrid route — route critical production traffic to dedicated, and lower priority to hosted. that gives predictable throughput while keeping costs lower.
[05:22] [05:27] Jordan: let's discuss benchmarks — priya, what will you run?
[05:30] Priya: i'll run three tests: single-request latency profile for 800–1k token outputs, throughput for concurrent 200 qps with 10ms inter-arrival to simulate spikes, and a batch job profile for offline summarization. i'll use Morningstar anonymized samples and our benchmarking harness (we'll share the script).
[05:52] Ravi: timeline for that?
[05:55] Priya: aim to have results in 7 business days after we get staging access and sample payloads. so target 2027-12-07.
[06:04] Elena: ok.
[06:05] [06:10] Aisha: about encryption — do you support envelope encryption and customer KMS for temp cache keys?
[06:15] Priya: yes envelope encryption is supported. for KV cache keys we can either manage them or use customer-managed keys; one nuance is cache rotation — we'll share patterns. sometimes the transciption (sic) of cache name is wrong but we mean KV cache.
[06:33] Tom: what about rollback/rollout — how do we do canaries?
[06:37] Marco: our rollout supports canaries by traffic percentage, model pinning, and automatic fallback to a pre-specified model variant on error thresholds. we can tie regressions to eval sets so we auto-alert if quality drops.
[06:52] Elena: would like automatic rollback if latency exceeds threshold during rollout.
[06:56] Priya: that's supported — set SLOs and we'll enforce routing to fallback. small caveat: if fallback model has different tokenization, results can change. we'll work with you to pin compatible variants.
[07:12] [07:18] Jordan: ok let's surface a few risks: data residency misconfiguration, longer-than-expected quantization regressions, and firewall misconfig. any other risks?
[07:26] Aisha: supply chain questions—what's your dependency patch cadence and do you publish SBOMs?
[07:32] Marco: we publish a weekly security digest and can produce an SBOM on request for enterprise customers. we'll include that in the security packet.
[07:44] Ravi: on integration specifics — do you provide SDKs or do we call REST endpoints?
[07:49] Priya: both. SDKs in Python/Node with streaming and function call hooks. we also support gRPC internally for higher throughput in private deployments.
[07:59] [08:05] Tom: okay i want to confirm network ports and a stub list we'll need to open.
[08:09] Priya: i'll put exact CIDRs and ports in the peering checklist doc but minimal ports are 443 outbound for control plane and the private endpoint ports we list. we'll send examples for transit gateway configs.
[08:22] Elena: one more item — we want to validate model quality with our clinical rubric. can priya ingest our rubric into the evals?
[08:29] Priya: yes, we can run your rubric as a test suite and produce diff reports. that will be part of the quality gate before canary.
[08:39] [08:42] Jordan: time check — we've got about 35 minutes left, open to deep-dive on any of these.
[08:47] Tom: i'd like a short deep dive on caching and batching behavior — specifically how prefix caching works for clinical notes.
[08:55] Priya: sure — short version: prefix/KV caching stores repeated context (e.g., system prompt, patient history) so subsequent requests reuse cached KV state. this reduces per-token compute. caveat: cache hit rate depends on request entropy; we can configure TTLs and patient-specific isolation. we also provide a cache eviction policy suited for regulated data.
[09:18] Ravi: when you say TTLs, is that per-tenant? we need per-patient isolation.
[09:23] Priya: yes we can scope caches per-tenant or per-user; for PHI we strongly recommend per-patient isolation and short TTL plus encryption at rest.
[09:33] Aisha: how do you handle audit log integrity? are logs append-only and can we ship them to our SIEM?
[09:40] Marco: logs are append-only, tamper-evident hash chains for enterprise packages, and yes we can forward to your SIEM via secure forwarder.
[09:52] [09:55] Elena: i'm worried about quantization impact on clinical hallucinations. can we gate quantization on evaluation thresholds?
[10:02] Priya: yes — we generally run a quantization shadow test: we serve on standard float baseline and run quantized variant in parallel, compare scores and only roll if metrics within tolerance. we'll include that in the pilot plan.
[10:20] Tom: ok that helps, thanks.
[10:23] [10:30] Jordan: near-term deliverables recap — Marco: security packet and pricing; Priya: benchmarking harness and peering checklist; Marco: schedule week 1 staging handoff; customer: payloads + network diagram. confirm timelines?
[10:45] Marco: i'll send schedule invites today and the security packet within 48 hours.
[10:49] Priya: i'll start the benchmark as soon as we get samples; target results by 2027-12-07.
[10:55] Ravi: we'll upload sample payloads by 2027-12-02 and share the tokenization mapping.
[11:00] Aisha: i'll provide the network diagram and firewall rules by 2027-12-03.
[11:06] Elena: ok let's do that.
[11:08] [11:12] Jordan: any other Qs?
[11:14] Speaker 1: um, is there an estimated cost for dedicated pool sizing? (voice overlaps)
[11:20] Marco: i'll include sizing options and cost bands in the security/ops packet.
[11:24] Tom: will there be a charge for extended log retention?
[11:27] Marco: yes it's an add-on — i'll detail tiers in the doc.
[11:30] [11:35] Elena: thanks everyone, this was productive. look forward to the packets.
[11:38] Jordan: thanks all — we'll follow up with notes and links. marco will drop invites.
[11:43] Priya: quick note — if you want a dedicated perf deep-dive next week, we can schedule a 90-minute sesh with our infra team.
[11:51] Tom: yes please, schedule that.
[11:54] Jordan: great. meeting adjourned.

Post-meeting notes: shared links to be sent — VPC peering checklist, benchmarking harness repo, security packet (SOC2, SBOM summary, KMS patterns), onboarding calendar invite for Week 1.

Transcript artifacts / imperfections: occasional mis-attribution, small transcript typos (quantizashun, KV cash), filler words removed sporadically.
